transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
Hello! I'm Dora, and I'm here to help answer any questions you might have about your cataract surgery or your recovery. 

Do you have anything you'd like to ask me about?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Hi Dora, yes, I do have a few questions. Firstly, when can I start doing a little bit of gardening?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
Great! So gardening is considered light exercise, which means you can start doing it after 1 week following your surgery.

Just remember to avoid any heavy lifting or strenuous work for about a month after your operation.

Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Thank you, that's helpful to know. I also wanted to ask, when can I start using my eye gel for dry eyes?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
That's a good question. If you were using eye gel for dry eyes before your operation, it's safe to continue using it now, unless you've been told otherwise by your care team.

Your medication and drops should be stored as directed on the bottle - so check whether it needs to go in the fridge or kept at room temperature.

Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Thanks for the information. I'm also feeling very sensitive to bright light lately. Is that normal?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.intended:
Yes, it is quite normal for your eyes to be a bit sensitive to light as they adjust to your new lenses.

If it's mild and things just seem brighter than you're used to, I'd recommend wearing sunglasses when you're outside. However, if you're experiencing significant pain in bright light, or if your eye is also red and painful, that's not normal and we may need to check that further.

Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Yes, I was wondering if I should still have some blurriness by now?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
It's quite common for vision to not be completely clear in the first week after surgery, and it should improve quickly and settle down over time.

How long ago was your surgery? If your vision is still blurry or getting significantly worse, we may need to check it to make sure everything's okay.

Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: No, I think that's everything for now. Thank you very much for your help, Dora!

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: You're welcome! Just to confirm - have all your questions been answered today?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Yes, you've answered all my questions. Thank you once again!

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: You're very welcome! I'm glad I could help. Take care, and wishing you a smooth recovery!
